variations.title: Granted host mapping
variations.scope: Source-supported mechanism. Access may predate workload compromise.

observations.relevance: Find the workload process that could use the mapping.
observations.establishes: A process episode was observed.
observations.limit: Process events alone do not resolve the object or establish a completed read.

observations.relevance: Observe the operation on a resolved host object through the mapping.
observations.establishes: A sufficiently scoped result supports a completed host read.
observations.limit: Path text and a mount declaration cannot establish object identity or source version.

observations.relevance: For a writable grant, compare independent state before and after use.
observations.establishes: A matching change supports a host mutation.
observations.limit: A read-only route can acquire data while leaving durable state unchanged.

observations.relevance: Compare the actual resource and action with intended policy.
observations.establishes: A relevant authorization record supports scope.
observations.limit: An approved backup can read the same object.

observations.relevance: Use a receiver-side witness for the designated representation.
observations.establishes: An exact receipt could support acquisition by the recipient.
observations.limit: Receipt alone leaves the original host version and workload cause unresolved.

claims.title: Occurred on a host-owned object
claims.qualification: The collector must retain a completed read or write and resolve the exact object, actor and version.

claims.title: Designated data reached this recipient
claims.qualification: Join the version-bound completed read to an independently scoped recipient.

claims.title: This use was outside intended policy
claims.qualification: Match identity, resource, action, and policy valid time.

variations.hunt: Hunt for high-risk host mappings, unusual resource access, or a workload near an independently observed host change.

variations.title: Namespace-mediated access
variations.scope: Source-supported namespace behavior. Individual fallback effects remain unresolved.

observations.relevance: Inspect the resulting actor and later child when PID context changes.
observations.establishes: A process lifetime can support the route when joined to the operation.
observations.limit: A named utility such as nsenter is a hunt lead. Its execution does not prove a successful transition.

observations.relevance: Resolve target namespace type, identity and signed result.
observations.establishes: An attributable successful operation supports a particular context change.
observations.limit: One changed namespace does not establish host resource access or effective host authority.

observations.relevance: Bind subsequent use of the relevant host resource.
observations.establishes: A completed, scoped operation could establish use.
observations.limit: A successful transition alone is upstream evidence.

observations.relevance: Check approved diagnostics, runtime work and node operations.
observations.establishes: Authorization can separate approved administration from a suspicious transition.
observations.limit: Local policy needs the exact actor and target.

observations.relevance: Corroborate a resulting host action.
observations.establishes: A qualified independent witness could support the outcome.
observations.limit: The public fallback narrative leaves individual transition-to-effect joins open.

claims.title: Relevant namespace transition occurred
claims.qualification: Require namespace type, real target, result, and workload lifetime. Generic process-only records cannot substitute.

claims.title: Host action followed this transition
claims.qualification: Qualify actual resulting authority, resulting actor and exact action. Evaluate policy separately.

variations.hunt: Hunt for unusual namespace tools, target selectors, and container-to-host process context. Approved node debugging can look similar.

variations.title: Privileged runtime delegation
variations.scope: Source-supported mechanism. A controller can act on a workload's behalf.

observations.relevance: Validate originating workload and resulting executor lifetimes.
observations.establishes: A boot-scoped process can be a join point.
observations.limit: A daemon's child or runtime event does not identify the initiating workload independently.

observations.relevance: Observe the controller's completed action on the target.
observations.establishes: A result tied to a resolved object supports use.
observations.limit: The actor on the host operation can be the controller rather than the requesting workload.

observations.relevance: Join authenticated requester, accepted request, terminal and realized host action.
observations.establishes: An exact terminal supports the scoped completed job.
observations.limit: Generic management audit or a mounted socket is insufficient. Abstract shim transport is a separate surface.

observations.relevance: Check intended authorization for the requesting actor and operation.
observations.establishes: An applicable policy can qualify approved or unauthorized use.
observations.limit: The controller's technical authority is separate from requester authorization.

observations.relevance: Verify the effect at the destination independently.
observations.establishes: A linked host witness can support the downstream effect.
observations.limit: An outcome may survive loss of workload attribution or upstream causal evidence.

claims.title: Host or destination effect can be investigated
claims.qualification: A qualified independent witness can establish the outcome within its scope; origin and policy remain open.

claims.title: Completed runtime job supports the witnessed effect
claims.qualification: Require a trusted terminal-to-object or result binding. Gate C.2 measured one instrumented helper contract only.

claims.title: Workload-to-effect link can be reconstructed
claims.qualification: Require the exact workload lifetime, job, target and outcome. Validate the crosswalk. Generic logs do not produce fixture transaction keys.

variations.hunt: Start with the process lifetime. If management audit is available, look for an unexpected create or a request to a host-enabled job.

variations.title: Runtime-materialized copy
variations.scope: Source-supported exposure. Later acquisition can be a local read.

observations.relevance: Identify the workload or later reader.
observations.establishes: A lifetime can help bind a local read.
observations.limit: A new process is not required to read an existing copy.

observations.relevance: Look for the original protected version at materialization.
observations.establishes: A trusted source-side record can bind that version.
observations.limit: The later reader may never touch the original host object.

observations.relevance: Trace runtime image-volume handling to the resulting copy.
observations.establishes: A captured transaction could identify materialization.
observations.limit: The advisory establishes capability; routine runtime lifecycle events do not guarantee provenance fields.

observations.relevance: Resolve the distinct local copy and its generation.
observations.establishes: A version-scoped identity can distinguish candidate copies.
observations.limit: Equal content may be stale or unrelated.

observations.relevance: Capture acquisition of the resulting representation.
observations.establishes: A recipient-bound read can support acquisition of the local copy.
observations.limit: A specific incident recipient and exact source-version link remain untested here.

claims.title: Workload acquired a local copy
claims.qualification: Require version-scoped local read and named recipient. This does not prove host provenance.

claims.title: The copy came from the designated host version
claims.qualification: A trusted materialization record must link the specific source version to the copy and recipient. Verify actual fields.

variations.hunt: Hunt unusual workload creation and volume handling. Investigate local reads without assuming a new host-side read.

variations.title: Runtime binary replacement
variations.scope: Source-supported lifecycle mechanism. Later use of the affected version is a separate claim.

observations.relevance: Find the later invocation that consumed the affected generation.
observations.establishes: An exact-generation launch can support execution.
observations.limit: An unrelated routine launch or a clean replacement may follow the alert.

observations.relevance: Scope the lifecycle event and affected runtime instance.
observations.establishes: A runtime action can establish the relevant stage.
observations.limit: Nearby runtime activity does not prove consumption.

observations.relevance: Observe a confirmed change to the exact host binary.
observations.establishes: Independent integrity evidence supports modification.
observations.limit: Approved package maintenance can replace the same artifact.

observations.relevance: Check whether this installer or actor had change approval.
observations.establishes: An approved change record can explain replacement.
observations.limit: Missing policy is unknown.

observations.relevance: Corroborate execution through a trusted witness when host trust is in doubt.
observations.establishes: An independent, qualified result could support host execution.
observations.limit: Binding to the affected generation remains necessary for causation.

claims.title: A host runtime binary changed
claims.qualification: Before/after identity or trusted integrity witness must identify the same target and generation.

claims.title: The affected generation ran under host authority
claims.qualification: Prove actual consumption and qualified authority. Check the authorized upgrade twin.

variations.hunt: Hunt unexpected runtime binary changes and nearby launches. Correlate by file generation before asserting causation.

variations.title: Device setup plus a daemon job
variations.scope: Source-supported composition. Exact downstream receipt is modeled.

observations.relevance: Check setup context and the effective resource view.
observations.establishes: Resolved context can support exposure investigation.
observations.limit: No explicit namespace change is required for socket reach.

observations.relevance: Observe the unintended mapping and exposed resource.
observations.establishes: The case demonstrates a read-only host view.
observations.limit: Read-only file semantics did not block Unix-socket use in that demonstration.

observations.relevance: Separate socket reach from the later privileged runtime job.
observations.establishes: A completed job can support utilization of daemon authority.
observations.limit: A file policy or removal of the conventional grant does not establish that this route is cut.

observations.relevance: Evaluate device setup policy and daemon job policy independently.
observations.establishes: Separate controls can cover distinct interactions.
observations.limit: Neither policy implies exact outcome or later acquisition.

observations.relevance: Watch delivery of the designated version from the job.
observations.establishes: A bound receipt could support the selected data objective.
observations.limit: Original device research supports the composition, not this modeled receipt.

claims.title: Unintended mapping and daemon reach were present
claims.qualification: Resolve actual mount scope and controller access. Read-only does not establish absence of socket activity.

claims.title: A host-enabled job used this composed route
claims.qualification: Join the originating setup, the authenticated job terminal, and actual host outcome.

variations.hunt: Hunt unusual setup changes and unexpected controller activity. Inspect separate enforcement at both boundaries.

variations.title: Effective local SSH trust
variations.scope: Source-supported resolver semantics. The workload-origin route is hypothetical.

observations.relevance: Identify the workload or authorized change actor.
observations.establishes: An actor lifetime supports attribution if the write is bound.
observations.limit: Process history cannot prove effective key eligibility.

observations.relevance: Check the changed input used for this account and connection.
observations.establishes: A qualified mutation can support the input change.
observations.limit: An ineffective write and an approved rotation are controls.

observations.relevance: Check approval, effective configuration and other providers.
observations.establishes: Applicable policy and trust inputs qualify the claim.
observations.limit: A central publisher can establish the same eligibility without a node escape.

observations.relevance: Check effective resolver decision and any later authentication separately.
observations.establishes: Qualified server-side evidence could establish eligibility.
observations.limit: A successful session may require other factors and is a separate result.

claims.title: A named key became eligible for this account
claims.qualification: Use exact account, key and connection context. Evaluate effective resolver and intended change policy separately.

claims.title: The workload caused the trust change
claims.qualification: Bind the exact trust input change or job to effective resolution and distinguish host-native or central issuance.

variations.hunt: Hunt trust source changes and destination authentication while the change origin is unresolved.

variations.title: Direct write diagnostic
variations.scope: Measured comparison of inert writers. Named hook and separate reference slots.

observations.relevance: The actor and fixture were enrolled for each diagnostic invocation.
observations.establishes: This supports scope for the comparison.
observations.limit: Actor matching does not fill an absent completion record.

observations.relevance: The selected Tetragon hook yielded zero returns for either tested vectored writer.
observations.establishes: This shows a scoped observation gap.
observations.limit: Reference tracing separately recorded the completed scalar, positional and both vectored writers. This does not imply general sensor incapability.

observations.relevance: The selected Tetragon hook retained both scalar and both positional returns.
observations.establishes: Captured signed returns support the tested operations. Separate witnesses observed canary changes.
observations.limit: The sensor projection lacked a native FD or durable object identifier. Separate invocations were used for reference and sensor.

observations.relevance: The independent witness observed the designated canary change.
observations.establishes: An independently supported outcome remained visible despite missing hook returns.
observations.limit: The outcome does not supply the missed operation or its exact actor/object binding.

claims.title: A controlled downstream state change was observed
claims.qualification: An independent scoped witness can support the fixture change even with the tested hook gap.

claims.title: Exact vectored completion from the selected hook
claims.qualification: Unavailable in the measured vectored arm. Selecting a generic kernel source cannot recover the missed record.

variations.hunt: Investigate the verified effect and check hook coverage across the applicable operation classes.

variations.title: Direct canary model • Gate B
variations.scope: Synthetic replay only. Scope and conclusion apply to the constructed fixture.

observations.relevance: The modeled workload identity gives scoped lifetime and policy context.
observations.establishes: The fixture provides scoped lifetime and policy context.
observations.limit: This says nothing about a native process collector.

observations.relevance: The fixture supplies targeted kernel evidence for the direct write.
observations.establishes: Under the modeled fields it supports completed direct use.
observations.limit: The modeled object/operation join is stronger than the measured Gate C direct evidence.

observations.relevance: The modeled W lens supplies intended-policy context.
observations.establishes: Authorized twins remain separate.
observations.limit: Policy alone cannot establish write completion.

observations.relevance: The modeled H lens supplies an independent canary result.
observations.establishes: It supports the scoped effect with modeled workload and kernel evidence.
observations.limit: No live sensor or actual escape validation follows.

claims.title: Direct canary effect can be confirmed in this model
claims.qualification: The Gate B modeled W/K/H set also requires exact workload incarnation. This profile choice only illustrates the evidence categories.

variations.hunt: Use the synthetic cases to test reasoning about missing evidence. Gate C found no qualifying direct measured combination.

evidenceExamples.title: Containerd task start
evidenceExamples.identifies: A containerd task start and a process/runtime join candidate.
evidenceExamples.establishes: The selected native lifecycle observer retained the start.
evidenceExamples.limits: A task start does not show a host operation, prove its origin, or establish a completed job.
evidenceExamples.strengthen: Join a boot-scoped workload lifetime and exact operation or job record.
evidenceExamples.administrative: Ordinary rollout, restart, or an approved troubleshooting workload.

evidenceExamples.title: Signed Tetragon return
evidenceExamples.identifies: The observed process and selected hook result in the test.
evidenceExamples.establishes: A scoped hook retained a positive byte return in this slot.
evidenceExamples.limits: A return alone does not prove exact target identity, filename provenance, independent change, or a workload-to-host link.
evidenceExamples.strengthen: Exact actor and object binding plus an independent witness. For mediation, retain the authorized request and terminal job relation.
evidenceExamples.administrative: A legitimate helper or maintenance service writing a host object.

evidenceExamples.title: Authenticated helper terminal
evidenceExamples.identifies: The fixture helper used the same scoped job for acceptance and completion. Job and actor values are withheld.
evidenceExamples.establishes: The instrumented helper reported a completed operation.
evidenceExamples.limits: This is a test harness record. A stock runtime log is not assumed to supply the same binding. A terminal is separate from an independent outcome.
evidenceExamples.strengthen: Join the exact fixture and terminal time to the independently read state, plus workload lifetime and policy for causal attribution.
evidenceExamples.administrative: An approved controller or broker operation can complete the same write.

evidenceExamples.title: Independent host state
evidenceExamples.identifies: The host-side witness for the inert state record.
evidenceExamples.establishes: Independently observed state changed within the fixture scope.
evidenceExamples.limits: The witness does not identify the writer, its permitted scope, or a preceding boundary crossing.
evidenceExamples.strengthen: Supply a completed operation or exact terminal, actor lifetime, object revision, and applicable authorization.
evidenceExamples.administrative: Authorized account, trust, schedule, or service maintenance can change the same category of state.

evidenceExamples.title: Direct effect with a modeled object binding
evidenceExamples.establishes: The full modeled direct evidence supports that synthetic effect.
evidenceExamples.limits: These are evidence categories, with no native event schema or measurement implied.
evidenceExamples.strengthen: Demonstrate actual collector support for actor, object generation, completion, and independent state.
evidenceExamples.administrative: A scoped authorized update can share the same observed shape.

findings.title: The effect can survive missing cause
findings.lead: D/H kept every witnessed delegated effect. Adding workload and policy context closed the causal links in this fixture.
findings.interpretation: D is the authenticated job and transaction evidence. H is the independent outcome. W gives workload lifetime and scope. A supplies the applicable policy. The W and A records help reconstruct which workload crossed which test boundary, even though the effect count stays the same.
findings.limitations: Eleven delegated trials included two attempts. The effect and causal denominators answer different questions. The cohort used inert records and a trusted test helper. It establishes neither successful escape nor real persistence.

findings.lensKey: D job · H outcome · W workload lifetime · A authorization

findings.title: A different write reaches the same canary
findings.cohort: Direct-write diagnostic; 8 reference slots and 8 separate sensor slots
findings.lead: The reference observer saw both vectored writers complete. The selected Tetragon hook missed both in separate runs.
findings.interpretation: Every diagnostic invocation changed its designated canary. A matching process and file alias did not recover the missed completion. The reference returns for each vectored writer were 16 bytes.
findings.limitations: The selected policy used vfs_write under the tested stack. Reference and Tetragon rows came from different invocations. The sensor projection lacked a native FD or durable object identifier. The result does not estimate broad collector coverage.

findings.title: One host effect, two attribution paths
findings.cohort: Primary canary positives and scoped controls
findings.lead: The modeled direct operation and delegated job reach an inert host canary. The smallest evidence sets distinguish which actor performed the operation.
findings.interpretation: For the direct path the kernel operation matters. For the delegated path, use the authenticated job. The independent outcome serves both. Gate B W includes workload and policy context.
findings.limitations: These minima use modeled identities and object bindings. They do not describe what an installed collector emits.

findings.title: The measured direct path lacked completion evidence
findings.cohort: Primary direct and delegated canary writes
findings.lead: The complete profile confirmed all primary delegated effects. It confirmed zero primary direct effects.
findings.interpretation: The complete profile's delegated minimum used workload, policy, authenticated helper and independent outcome records. The selected native hook provided no completed direct operation.
findings.limitations: No measured combination qualified for direct or combined coverage, and none qualified in the native profiles. Two additional delayed delegated positives are outside the primary denominator.

minima.scope: Every cutoff in complete instrumentation, specific to the tested helper.

placements.title: Dangerous exposure
placements.detection: Admission or inventory shows an unexpected grant.
placements.prevention: Scope admission, grants and versions before use.
placements.deception: An isolated nonfunctional management surface can show unexpected contact.
placements.investigation: Check approved debug and device workloads.

placements.title: Boundary interaction
placements.detection: Qualify target context, resolved object or controller peer.
placements.prevention: Enforce the specific boundary before the operation.
placements.deception: Record contact with an inert decoy without granting real authority.
placements.investigation: Bind actor lifetime, target identity and result.

placements.title: Exercise of authority
placements.detection: Follow a completed read, write, or host-enabled job.
placements.prevention: Restrict the job or allowed resource operation where eligible.
placements.deception: Track use of an isolated nonsecret marker.
placements.investigation: Separate request acceptance, completion and actual authorized scope.

placements.title: Downstream effect
placements.detection: Check the independent recipient, execution or trust witness.
placements.deception: Observe effects on a controlled decoy state.
placements.investigation: Record the effect even if origin and causal edge remain open.

placements.title: Subsequent use
placements.detection: Watch later authentication, code consumption or relevant destination activity.
placements.prevention: Apply destination access and redemption policy.
placements.deception: Inert decoy use can provide a distinct signal.
placements.investigation: Link the later outcome to the exact credential, code generation or prior action.
